slowdown.note: In his 2 October 2026 Fox News op-ed he calls for a worldwide pause on recursive self-improvement and a global pause on superintelligence, for safety reasons; a call to pause for safety counts as yes here.

pause.note: He calls for a 'global pause on superintelligence' and a worldwide pause on recursive self-improvement, framed as pillars of a U.S.-China treaty, so the pause is conditional on international agreement.

intl.note: He calls for a binding U.S.-China AI treaty whose first pillar is a worldwide pause on recursive self-improvement, and (per Axios, not opened) set out five provisions for such an agreement in a letter to Secretary of State Rubio.

rsi.note: He announced a planned Human Control Over AI Act that would bar AI systems that recursively self-improve until a federal agency and safeguards exist, and called for a worldwide pause on recursive self-improvement. Whether the bill has been formally introduced was not confirmed.

record: Announced a planned Human Control Over AI Act banning recursively self-improving AI until federal safeguards exist and creating a federal agency to license frontier models (formal introduction not confirmed).

Letter to Secretary of State Rubio proposing a U.S.-China AI agreement including pauses on recursive self-improvement and superintelligence, pre-release audits, kill-switch protocols and inspection regimes (reported; page not opened).

Letters to Chinese AI companies (DeepSeek, Alibaba, Moonshot AI) asking for documents on their work toward superintelligence and recursive self-improvement (reported in search results only; not opened).
Letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick on the lack of permanent leadership at the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (not opened; mainly about China and model evaluation).
House Select Committee on the CCP Democrats press release, 2026-08-13
grade_reason: In September and October 2026 he said in his own words that AI poses a 'civilizational extinction risk' and that self-improving AI is the most likely path to humanity losing control of the technology. No dismissive statement was found.
notes: Seven web searches ran; none were refused. Quotes were read on the pages linked, but the page-reading tool returned short excerpts, so a reviewer should confirm exact wording, especially the Fox News op-ed (fetched via its print view) and the CNBC quotes, which were read in secondary reports (The Next Web, Common Dreams), not on CNBC itself. Axios (2026-09-25) and South China Morning Post pages returned 403 and were not read. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: Crypto Briefing says he 'has publicly supported' it, but no source showed him as a sponsor or co-sponsor, so it is not recorded. Paraphrases left out: Axios (23 Aug 2026) reports he supports a pause on data center construction in Pennsylvania, Michigan and Wisconsin (motivation not tied to AI risk in what I saw, so not a slowdown position); Fox op-ed also says an AI war 'is catastrophic for civilization' and superintelligence 'could unleash Pandora's box' (not added as separate statements). The many-signer House letters were not searched, per instructions. Introduction status of the Human Control Over AI Act is unverified.
